newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl government popularity at three-year low - poll.
newsitem.headline: Kohl government popularity at three-year low - poll.

text.p: The German government has fallen to its lowest popularity level since the 1994 general election, according to an opinion poll on Friday.

ZDF television's monthly Politbarometer survey showed 58 percent of the 1,285 Germans polled were dissatisfied with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government and only 36 percent said it was doing a good job.
The opposition Social Democrats (SPD), however, did not present a convincing alternative for most of those polled -- only 17 percent thought they would do better in power.
The poll also reported widespread disillusion -- sixty percent said it made no difference whether the opposition or Kohl's coalition were in power.
"Despite its low rating the government would be far ahead in a general election," ZDF said.
The survey showed that Kohl's Christian Democrat coalition (CDU/CSU) with liberal Free Democrats scored 47 percent against a potential coalition of SPD and Greens with 45 percent.
Unemployment was the most important issue in Germany for 82 percent of those polled.
"More people than ever think it will be impossible to halve unemployment by the year 2000," ZDF said, referring to one the German government's stated aims.

Those polled were pessimistic about the economy and its prospects for improvement. Only 12 percent thought it would improve, while 42 percent expected no change and 45 percent said it could only get worse.
Only eight percent were happy with the state of the economy, 55 percent said it was "so-so" and 39 percent complained it was in bad shape.
